TV-1.note: key-publish: Alice publishes her Ed25519 key; this = says = SHA-256(pub); the envelope carries pub

TV-2.note: self: label Alice, uses [statements], controller person (a self-claim)

TV-3.note: define: Alice publishes definition DV-1 by its DefinitionId

TV-4.note: attestation about an ARTIFACT digest (not a key): build-provenance = reproducible

TV-5.note: trust: Carol trusts Alice about build-provenance in {reproducible, attested}; may delegate depth 1 within {reproducible}

TV-6.note: review: Bob reviews statement TV-4 (target is a statement digest): outcome approve

TV-7.note: revoke: Alice revokes TV-4 by digest, effective 2026-10-21

TV-8.note: rotate: Bob's old key names its successor; valid.issued orders statements around the rotation

TV-9.note: trust, threshold form: Carol trusts any 2 of {Alice, Bob, Dave}; this is absent; k = 2, n = 3

TV-10.note: trust, threshold form at the upper bound: k = n = 3

TV-11.note: trust, threshold form at the lower bound: k = 1, and the fewest members allowed, n = 2

TV-12.note: define: Alice publishes definition DV-2 by its DefinitionId

TV-13.note: attestation about a KEY: Alice says Bob's key has name "fred" (the NameCert role, ARCH-0002 P6)

TV-14.note: trust: Alice trusts Bob about build-provenance in {attested}; outside TV-5's may-delegate ranges, so widening (SPEC-0004 §6.3 item 4)

TV-15.note: attestation: Bob says the artifact's build-provenance is attested

TV-16.note: trust: Alice trusts Bob about build-provenance in {reproducible}, no may-delegate: within TV-5, one hop only

TV-17.note: attestation: Bob says the artifact's build-provenance is reproducible

TV-18.note: trust: Bob trusts Dave about build-provenance in {reproducible}; Bob holds no delegation, so depth (§6.3 item 3)

TV-19.note: attestation: Dave says the artifact's build-provenance is reproducible

TV-20.note: trust: Alice trusts Bob about {reproducible} with may-delegate depth 1; TV-5 left Alice depth 1, so at most 0 may pass on: widening (§6.3 item 6)

TV-21.note: define: Dave, the library lead, publishes definition DV-3 `library-review`

TV-22.note: trust: Carol, a reader, trusts Dave about reviewed (unbounded), may delegate depth 1; her anchor in context `library`

TV-23.note: trust: Dave delegates reviewed in {partial} to Bob, a student reviewer

TV-24.note: attestation: Bob says the record has reviewed = yes, from template record-reviewed; outside his scope

TV-25.note: attestation: Bob says the record has reviewed = partial, from template record-reviewed

TV-26.note: attestation about a DESCRIPTION target (R-M-11): Dave says the work titled "Simple Public Key Certificate" is reviewed = yes; its locator rides as an attribute

TV-27.note: define: Alice publishes definition DV-4 `naming`, whose `name` type has base kind name

TV-28.note: name binding: Alice's fred is Bob's key (one hop; SPEC-0004 §5.3)

TV-29.note: name binding: Bob's sam is Dave's key; with TV-28, Alice's fred's sam is Dave (a compound name)

TV-30.note: name binding to a NAME target (SPEC-0002 §7.2 type 7): Carol's builder is Alice's fred's sam

TV-31.note: trust to a NAME: Carol trusts Carol's builder about build-provenance in {reproducible}, one hop

TV-32.note: name binding: Bob's fred is Dave's key. It is in Bob's namespace, never Alice's

TV-33.note: name binding: Alice's loop is Alice's loop, a cycle

TV-34.note: name binding: Alice's fred is also Dave's key; with TV-28, Alice's fred is the set {Bob, Dave}

N-1.why: TBS map keys are not in deterministic order; the signature over those bytes is valid

N-3.why: outer says (Bob) does not equal inner says (Alice)

N-4.why: public key is a small-order point (the identity); MUST be rejected before any verification

N-5.why: signature S >= L (malleated); MUST be rejected even though R and the equation may verify

N-6.why: TBS contains a floating-point value; outside the KSA data model

N-7.why: threshold form with k = 0, below the range 1 <= k <= n

N-8.why: threshold form with k = 4 and n = 3, above the range 1 <= k <= n

N-9.why: n = 4 beside three members needs a body field that does not exist; closed map

N-10.why: the array head of trusts says n = 4 and three members follow; not well-formed CBOR, correctly signed

N-11.why: attestation whose target is a bare locator [5, uri]; target type 5 is reserved, so no digest is bound

N-12.why: name target with an empty label list; a name has at least one label

N-13.why: name target whose label "Fred" is outside [a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}

E-1.note: a hop's about [attested] is not within the delegator's may-delegate ranges [reproducible]

E-2.note: TV-5 → TV-16: one hop within ranges; Bob may attest

E-3.note: TV-16 carries no may-delegate, so Bob's own trust statement is not followed

E-4.note: TV-20 asks for depth 1 where at most 0 remains; widening fails the hop, it is not clipped to 0

E-5.note: TV-22 → TV-23: Bob is within scope for partial

E-6.note: UC-3's must-fail: Bob, delegated only {partial}, asserts yes

E-7.note: Dave, anchored directly, attests a description target

R-2.note: a compound name: Alice's fred is Bob, Bob's sam is Dave

R-3.note: a binding to a name: Carol's builder is Alice's fred's sam

R-4.note: two bindings of one label: the name is a set (SDSI group), not an error

R-5.note: missing link: Bob binds no sam

R-6.note: Alice's loop is defined as itself

R-7.note: the only fred binding is Bob's; Bob cannot bind a label in Alice's namespace

E-8.note: TV-31 trusts Carol's builder, which resolves to Dave (R-3); Dave attests

E-9.note: without TV-29 Carol's builder resolves to no key, so TV-31 starts no path

E-10.note: Bob is Alice's fred, not Carol's builder: a name grants nothing to the keys it passes through
